messages:
maria: FYI dashboards are showing a big jump in FCP/TTI after this morning's frontend deploy. Users hitting the main billing dashboard see 2–3s slower interactive time.
kai: Seen it too. Trace looks like chart widgets blocking main thread during hydration — lots of layout thrash when many series are present.
sam: Repro steps: open /console/billing with 50+ series, scroll, then click a metric. CPU goes to 100% and charts freeze for ~1.5s. I recorded a flamechart.
ada: Can you paste the top frames? Is it our code or the new chart library (visx -> chartly upgrade)?
sam: Top frames point to chartly's render + our formatSeries() call. formatSeries is doing expensive date parsing per point.
leigh: formatSeries was simplified in the PR but we kept parsing in JS instead of using preprocessed timestamps. Probably repeated Date() calls.
maria: Oof. That PR also added heavier SVG markers and per-point aria attributes. Bundle size also bumped ~80KB gz.
oliver: deploy-bot reported a canary rollout at 06:12 (10% traffic). Canary logs show 10x more longtasks for users routed to canary.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout step: traffic=10% -> health checks OK -> monitoring flagged longtask_rate > threshold -> alert created.
kai: Two immediate mitigations: 1) revert chartly change in canary; 2) lazy-hydrate widgets below the fold. Which is faster to ship?
ad a: Revert is fastest for perf but kills the chart improvements. Lazy-hydration needs small runtime change but safer for UX.
maria: Also we should reduce telemetry sampling for devtools events — current sampling emits full series histograms per chart action, blowing up telemetry ingestion and adding CPU on client.
sam: Agree. Set sampling to 10% for hist events and send aggregations server-side. Also push date parsing into the build step (pre-serialize timestamps as numbers).
leigh: I have a patch that moves parse to build; it's tiny. But it doesn't fix SVG/marker overhead.
oliver: I'll flip canary back if we think rollback is required. Any objections to pausing canary now and shipping the parse/build patch asap?
kai: Pause canary yes. Ship parse/build + telemetry sampling change as hotfix to canary before unpausing.
maria: Another thought — move heavy rendering to an offscreen canvas / web worker and fallback to SVG for older browsers. That'd reduce main-thread longtasks.
ad a: Worth a spike but too big for hotfix.
sam: For immediate fix I'll open PR to: 1) change Date parsing to unix ms in build; 2) reduce telemetry hist sample to 10%; 3) add an experiment flag to disable SVG markers per-user.
maria: Perfect. After PR we can re-run load test and canary. If canary is green, we can reintroduce chartly in smaller steps (no markers, no per-point aria).
oliver: Action items: @sam PR now, @leigh validate build change, @ada spike webworker POC next week. I'll pause canary. Anyone want me to revert completely instead?
kai: Pause + hotfix path is least disruptive.
maria: Thanks. Also log this in the incident channel with perf tag so CS knows.
oliver: Done. Paused canary at 07:15 and filed incident: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-124
sam: PR opened: https://git.redwood/console/pull/4021 — contains parse/build + telemetry sampling. Running CI.
leigh: Verified build-time parse in my local bundle — initial JS down ~40ms parsing cost on big dashboard.
maria: Great. We'll monitor metrics (FCP, longtask rate, telemetry ingestion) and follow up in the morning.
ada: Small note—remember to bump release notes: "Reverted chartly upgrade due to perf; temporary telemetry sampling change" :memo:
maria: Yup.
oliver: Thanks team :thumbsup:
